BLOCKER: EDP-16 declares objpolicy the "ONE minting boundary", "wired by objpolicy.HTTPMiddleware with a credential-validating resolver", but the diff ships no caller of `Mint`/`HTTPMiddleware` and migrates no existing signed-URL path — the documented control is not actually in force.
Reconciliation scanner and signed-URL policy are shipped as libraries with no entrypoint, no wiring and no consumer; the decision record asserts operational controls that the code does not provide.
MAJOR: `objreconcile.MaxObjects` is checked only *after* `store.List` has already materialised the full slice; the stated "fail closed rather than OOM" bound does not actually bound memory.

`Scan` issues one sequential `Head` per expected key (up to 100k) with no concurrency/pagination; S3 `List` never carries checksums, so every manifest entry costs a round trip — the scanner is unusable at its own stated bound.
`S3Store.Capabilities()` hardcodes `ObjectVersioning: true` while `Put` gates `Immutable` on the probed `s.versioned` — capability advertisement contradicts enforcement.

`New()` swallows `probeLock`/`probeVersioning` errors (log only); a permissions/network failure at startup permanently degrades the store to "no object lock", so retention fails at request time instead of failing fast at construction.

Reconcile double-reports: a manifest entry with a malformed checksum is classified `Invalid`, excluded from `want`, and its real store object is then additionally reported `Orphaned` — an untrustworthy report that invites a destructive "repair".
`LocalStore.Put` enforces `Immutable` only when existing meta has a non-empty `Checksum`; objects without a stored checksum are silently overwritable — `Immutable` fails open.

`s3store.Delete` and `stat` now map missing keys to `os.ErrNotExist`: an unannounced behaviour change to existing public API for idempotent-delete callers, not covered by the AC and with no migration note.
`objstore_test.go` newly calls `errors.Is` but the diff does not add an `errors` import — verify the module builds before merge.

`objpolicy.stats.byReason` (keyed by tenant) and `LocalStore.keyLocks` (keyed by object) are unbounded process-global maps with no eviction; long-lived multi-tenant processes grow without bound and are trivially inflatable.

`datastore.Lifecycle()` requires both `Capabilities().ObjectLock` *and* the `LifecycleCapable` assertion — two sources of truth: S3 can advertise lock support while `ObjectLifecycle` errors, and a `LifecycleCapable` provider is hidden when its probe fails.
MINOR: Local `Immutable` check runs only after the full body is streamed and hashed into tmp; rejection is not fail-fast and wastes I/O on hostile input.
`ApplyLifecycle` with an empty policy (no mode, no hold) is a silent no-op returning nil — callers get no signal that nothing was applied.
`ApplyLifecycle` lazily re-probes object lock but `Put` never re-probes versioning; `objectLock` is set true once and never invalidated if bucket config changes — inconsistent refresh policy.
`cleanPath` silently collapses `//` and `.` segments, so a URL can be minted for a key different from the caller-supplied string; canonicalisation should be detected and rejected, not rewritten.
`objpolicy` uses stdlib `log` and process-global state rather than an injectable, metric-emitting sink; no metrics hook for denials, and tenant IDs appear in logs.
`ComplianceOptIn`/`RetentionMode` are duplicated across `PutOptions` and `LifecyclePolicy`; one shared policy type would prevent drift.
The COMPLIANCE "cannot be shortened or released" invariant is enforced only by S3 — no client-side guard or test covers it.
Reconciliation drift surfaces only via `log.Printf`; no metric, exit-code contract, or report sink, so drift is not observable by ops.
NIT: `ErrUnsupported` re-exported as a package-level var in `objpolicy` invites divergence from `datastore.ErrUnsupported`.
`errLocalLifecycle` is a shared package-level error instance returned by every call; return a fresh `UnsupportedError` for per-call diagnostics.
`PartialApplyError.Applied` is a free-form string; use typed constants.
New modules hardcode `go 1.21` — confirm against the repo toolchain directive.
SUMMARY: Capability-shaped design is sound (optional `LifecycleCapable`, typed errors, explicit COMPLIANCE opt-in, read-only deterministic reconcile) with good unit coverage.

Top risks: the "single signed-URL minting boundary" is documented but not wired anywhere, so the control is aspirational; the reconcile memory bound and N+1 HEAD pattern do not scale; S3 capability advertisement and swallowed probe failures can silently degrade compliance enforcement.
Recommend wiring at least one real call path and fixing the report double-counting before this is treated as a shipped control.
